children: Over 500 participants join community initiative encouraging regular exercise, preventive screening and healthier everyday habits

HCG Suchirayu Hospital Hubballi organised a World Heart Day walkathon that brought together more than 500 participants to promote cardiovascular health, preventive care and regular physical activity. Held under the theme “Adjust Maadbedi, Walk Madi, Care Madi,” the initiative encouraged residents to incorporate movement into their daily routines and adopt healthier heart-care practices.

The event was attended by Shri Prasad Abbayya, MLA, Hubballi-Dharwad East Assembly Constituency, as Chief Guest, along with Shri Borase Bhushan Gulabrao, IPS, Deputy Inspector General of Police and Commissioner of Police, Hubballi-Dharwad District, and Dr Parshuram F.K., District Health Officer, Dharwad District, as Guests of Honour.

Shri Prasad Abbayya said, “A healthy community begins with healthy individuals, and initiatives like this encourage people to take greater responsibility for their well-being. It is heartening to see citizens come together for a cause that promotes a healthier and more active Hubballi-Dharwad.” Shri Borase Bhushan Gulabrao highlighted walking as an accessible form of physical activity, while Dr Parshuram F.K. stressed the importance of sustained community participation in preventive healthcare.

Dr Narendra Hiregoudar, Senior Interventional Cardiologist, HCG Suchirayu Hospital, Hubballi, said, “Heart health is closely linked to the choices we make every day. Regular physical activity, a balanced diet and timely monitoring of risk factors such as blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol can play an important role in preventing cardiovascular disease.”

Dr Sharan Hallad, Senior CTVS Surgeon, HCG Suchirayu Hospital, added that prevention remains important despite advances in cardiac treatment, urging people to recognise warning signs and understand individual risk factors.

Dr Ameet Sattur, Senior Interventional Cardiologist, HCG Suchirayu Hospital, said, “Heart disease can develop silently, which is why people should not wait for symptoms before thinking about their cardiovascular health.

Regular screening and consistent lifestyle changes can help identify and manage risks early.”  The walkathon was organised in association with the Indian Medical Association, State Bank of India, District Health Officer, Dharwad, Deshpande Foundation, Lions Club, Obsession Run Club, Ayush Federation of India, Dharwad, Sanjeevani Ayurveda Medical College and Hospital, Hubballi, and Radio Mirchi 98.3 FM. Participants were also offered free health check-ups and health coupons, reinforcing the importance of preventive screening. The event concluded with refreshments and breakfast for participants.
